info.desc: Some Girls is an album by The Rolling Stones, released in 1978. Considered a highlight of their output and the best of their post-Exile on Main St. records, the album revitalized the band's career upon its release and re-established The Rolling Stones as a vital rock and roll band in an era infused with punk rock and disco. It also became the band's biggest-selling album in the United States, with more than six million copies to date. With the advent of punk rock, The Rolling Stones, among many of their musical contemporaries, were being targeted by some in the movement .

podcast.body: This album was a crucial turning point in the band's career, released in 1978 after a decade of critically indifferent albums that had led them to be labeled "rock dinosaurs." It was an effort to regain critical acclaim and reassert their status. Keith Richards contributed minimally due to a pending drug trial in Canada, leaving Mick Jagger to largely compose it solo. The album incorporated strong influences from disco and punk, current genres at the time, blending them with their classic rock sound. It achieved tremendous critical and commercial success and is now considered their second-best album after "Exile on Main St." "Este disco es alucinante, fue un punto muy importante dentro de la carrera de los Rolling Stones."
